summary: The domain follows the ISA-95 functional hierarchy. Levels 1 and 2 (controller, robot, supervisory and process control) use IEC 61131-3, ISA-101, ISA-18.2 and ISA-88. Level 3 operations (execution, scheduling, quality, metrology) follow the IEC 62264-3 activity model, MESA-11 and the APICS planning functions. Before these sit manufacturing engineering (process planning, factory design) and machine-program preparation, which is split the way CAM modules and post-processors are sold: milling by axis count, turning and mill-turn, sheet and profile cutting with nesting (cutting-and-packing typology), NC post-processing and verification, and additive build preparation by ISO/ASTM 52900 process category.

capabilities.name: Manufacturing process planning
capabilities.definition: Given a product design and the plant's resources, decide how it will be made: operations and their order, machines, setups, tooling, routing and expected cost.

crosswalk.label: Mechanical product definition for process planning using machining features

capabilities.notes: New capability, not a seed. Split out of the CAM and MES seeds because planning how to make a part (operations, setups, routing, cost) comes before and is independent of toolpath generation and of execution; ISA-95 treats it as product definition management.

tasks.name: Machining process plan generation
tasks.definition: Given a part model with features and tolerances, stock and available machines, produce setups, operation sequence and machine, fixture and tool assignments.
tasks.inputs: part model with machining features and tolerances, stock, machine and tooling catalogue
tasks.outputs: process plan: setups, ordered operations, resource assignments
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: setup count, tool changes and estimated machining time can be scored on shared test parts, but no standard suite exists

tasks.name: Manufacturing bill and routing authoring
tasks.definition: Given an engineering bill of materials and plant layout, produce a manufacturing bill of materials grouped by station and a routing of operations with work centres and standard times.
tasks.inputs: engineering bill of materials, plant work centres, standard times
tasks.outputs: manufacturing bill of materials, routing (bill of process)
tasks.benchmarkable: no: correct structure depends on plant conventions and there is no reference data

tasks.name: Work instruction authoring
tasks.definition: Given a process plan, 3D models and quality requirements, produce step-by-step operator instructions with visuals, parameters and checks.
tasks.inputs: process plan, product models, quality checks
tasks.outputs: illustrated work instructions per station
tasks.benchmarkable: no: quality is judged by operators and there is no benchmark
tasks.notes: Delivery of instructions at the station is under produce.manufacturing_execution.execution_guidance.

tasks.name: Manufacturing cost estimation
tasks.definition: Given a part model or drawing, material, process route and shop rates, estimate cycle time, piece cost and tooling cost.
tasks.inputs: part model or drawing, material, process route, machine and labour rates
tasks.outputs: cycle-time and cost estimate, quote
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: estimates can be scored against actual costed jobs, but such data are private

tasks.name: Cutting tool and cutting data management
tasks.definition: Given tool assemblies, workpiece materials and machines, maintain the tool library and compute recommended speeds, feeds and tool life.
tasks.inputs: tool components and assemblies, workpiece material, machine limits
tasks.outputs: tool library records, cutting parameters, expected tool life

crosswalk.label: Cutting tool data representation and exchange

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: recommended cutting data can be checked against measured tool life and force data, which are scarce

capabilities.name: Milling toolpath programming
capabilities.definition: Given part and stock geometry, fixtures, cutting tools and the machine's axis configuration, generate collision-free milling toolpaths that bring the stock to the part within tolerance.
onet_categories: Computer aided design CAD and computer aided manufacturing CAM system
capabilities.notes: Was part of seed 'CNC toolpath planning and post-processing (CAM), nesting'. CAM is split by process the way CAM modules and post-processors are sold (mill, lathe/mill-turn, wire and profile, router); milling is further split by axis count (2.5, 3, 3+2, 4, 5) because each step changes the geometry problem and the post-processor.

tasks.name: 2.5-axis milling
tasks.definition: Given 2D profiles or prismatic features with depths, generate contouring, pocketing, facing, slotting, chamfering and engraving paths at discrete Z levels.
tasks.inputs: 2D profiles or prismatic features, depths, tools, stock, fixture
tasks.outputs: cutter location path or controller code

crosswalk.label: Planar face, pocket, slot and profile features

onet_products: Computer aided design and computer aided manufacturing CAD/CAM engraving software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: machining time, air-cutting fraction and gouge-free coverage are computable by stock simulation on shared prismatic parts; config/capabilities.csv already lists cam-bench for CAM
tasks.notes: Includes panel routing for woodworking and sign engraving, which are 2.5-axis milling with process-specific tooling.

tasks.name: Hole-making cycles
tasks.definition: Given hole features (diameter, depth, thread, tolerance), choose drilling, peck, tapping, boring, reaming or thread-milling cycles and an efficient visiting order.
tasks.inputs: hole features, tools, machine canned-cycle set
tasks.outputs: ordered hole operations with canned cycles
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: cycle choice can be checked against thread and depth specifications and the visiting order is a travelling-salesman instance

tasks.name: Three-axis surface roughing
tasks.definition: Given 3D part and stock, remove bulk material with constant-engagement (adaptive, trochoidal) or Z-level clearing, leaving uniform stock for finishing.
tasks.inputs: part surfaces, stock model, tools and holders, engagement limits
tasks.outputs: roughing toolpath, remaining stock model
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: removal rate, engagement violations and remaining stock are computable by stock simulation on reference parts

tasks.name: Three-axis surface finishing
tasks.definition: Given freeform surfaces and remaining stock, generate parallel, waterline, scallop, pencil and rest-machining passes that meet a scallop-height and surface tolerance.
tasks.inputs: part surfaces, remaining stock, ball or bull-nose tools, tolerance, scallop height
tasks.outputs: finishing toolpaths
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: scallop height, gouges and deviation from the design surface are computable from simulated stock

tasks.name: Indexed five-axis (3+2) milling
tasks.definition: Given a part on a rotary-tilting machine, choose fixed tool orientations that reach all features in few setups, and generate three-axis paths in each tilted work plane.
tasks.inputs: part model, machine rotary limits, fixture, tools
tasks.outputs: set of tool orientations and per-plane toolpaths
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: number of orientations and feature accessibility are scoreable; tilted-plane output must be checked by machine simulation

tasks.name: Simultaneous four-axis rotary milling
tasks.definition: Given a part machined around one rotary axis, generate wrapped and rotary-contouring paths that move the rotary axis during cutting.
tasks.inputs: part model, rotary axis definition, tools
tasks.outputs: four-axis toolpath
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: wrap accuracy is checkable by simulation but few reference parts exist

tasks.name: Simultaneous five-axis milling
tasks.definition: Given freeform or ruled surfaces, generate paths with a continuously varying tool axis (swarf, flowline, impeller, port) that avoid holder and spindle collisions and keep the axis smooth.
tasks.inputs: part surfaces, tools and holders, machine kinematics and limits
tasks.outputs: five-axis toolpath with tool-axis vectors

crosswalk.label: Machining test pieces including the cone frustum for five-axis machines

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the ISO 10791-7 cone frustum and similar test pieces give reference geometry; gouges, collisions and axis reversals are measurable in simulation

tasks.name: Feature-based automatic programming
tasks.definition: Given a solid model, recognize machining features and apply stored strategies to produce a complete program with little manual input.
tasks.inputs: solid model, feature-strategy knowledge base, tools, machine
tasks.outputs: recognized features and complete toolpath set
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: feature recognition is scoreable on labelled CAD sets (MFCAD, MFCAD++) and the resulting programs by stock simulation
tasks.notes: Dental restoration CAM sits here: it is automated strategy selection on a fixed part family.

capabilities.name: Turning, mill-turn and grinding programming
capabilities.definition: Given a rotational part, bar or blank stock and a lathe, multitasking or grinding machine configuration, generate synchronized programs for its spindles, turrets and axes.
capabilities.notes: Split from the CAM seed. Lathe, mill-turn and Swiss machines are separate CAM modules and separate post-processors because channel synchronization and live tooling change the problem. Tool grinding is placed here as the other rotational-part process with its own programming software.

tasks.name: Two-axis turning
tasks.definition: Given a turned profile and stock, generate facing, OD and ID roughing and finishing, grooving, threading and parting with tool-nose compensation.
tasks.inputs: rotational profile, stock, turning tools
tasks.outputs: lathe program
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: cycle time and profile deviation after simulated cutting are scoreable on reference turned parts

tasks.name: Live-tool C and Y-axis milling
tasks.definition: Given a turned part with flats, cross holes and slots, generate milling on a lathe using polar or cylindrical interpolation with the C axis and optional Y axis.
tasks.inputs: part model, lathe with live tools, C and Y axis limits
tasks.outputs: combined turning and milling program
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: verifiable only by machine simulation with the specific turret and spindle model

tasks.name: B-axis mill-turn multitasking
tasks.definition: Given a complex part on a machine with a tilting milling head, main and sub-spindles, order turning and multi-axis milling operations and spindle transfers.
tasks.inputs: part model, multitasking machine model, tools
tasks.outputs: multitasking program with transfers
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: needs full machine kinematic models; cycle time and collisions are measurable in simulation

tasks.name: Multi-channel and Swiss-type synchronization
tasks.definition: Given operations for a sliding-headstock or twin-turret lathe, assign them to channels, insert wait and sync codes and balance the cycle.
tasks.inputs: operation list, machine channels, turrets and spindles
tasks.outputs: synchronized multi-channel program and timing chart
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: channel balancing is a scheduling problem and sync validity is checkable in simulation, but machine models are proprietary

tasks.name: Tool and cutter grinding programming
tasks.definition: Given a cutter specification (flutes, helix, rake, relief, point), generate wheel paths for a multi-axis tool grinder.
tasks.inputs: cutter geometry, wheel set, grinder kinematics
tasks.outputs: grinding program and simulated tool geometry
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: the simulated ground geometry can be compared with the specification, but grinder models are machine-specific

capabilities.name: Sheet and profile cutting programming
capabilities.definition: Given flat, linear or tubular stock and part outlines or sheet-metal models, lay parts out on the stock and generate cutting, punching, bending or wire-erosion programs.

crosswalk.scheme: Waescher et al. 2007 cutting and packing typology
crosswalk.label: Cutting and packing problems (cutting stock, knapsack, open dimension; one- and two-dimensional, regular and irregular)

capabilities.notes: Holds the 'nesting' part of the CAM seed. Nesting tasks follow the Waescher typology (dimension and shape of items), which is also how the benchmark literature is organized; cutting, punching and bending follow the machine types that sheet-metal CAM is sold for.

tasks.name: Two-dimensional profile cutting paths
tasks.definition: Given nested part outlines and a laser, plasma, oxyfuel, waterjet or knife cutter, generate cut paths with lead-ins, kerf compensation, pierce points, micro-joints and a cut order that limits heat and tip-up.
tasks.inputs: nested layout, cutting process and machine parameters
tasks.outputs: cutting program
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: cut length, pierce count and rapid travel are scoreable; cut quality is not

tasks.name: Irregular nesting on sheet and plate
tasks.definition: Given irregular part shapes, quantities and sheets or plates, place parts with allowed rotations to maximize utilization, using common-line cutting and part-in-part where possible.
tasks.inputs: part outlines, quantities, rotation rules, sheet sizes and remnants
tasks.outputs: nested layouts, utilization, remnant definitions

crosswalk.scheme: Waescher et al. 2007 cutting and packing typology
crosswalk.label: Two-dimensional irregular cutting stock and open dimension problems

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ESICUP irregular nesting instances (albano, dagli, jakobs, shapes, swim) have best-known utilizations

tasks.name: Rectangular and guillotine panel cutting
tasks.definition: Given rectangular parts and boards or glass sheets, generate cutting patterns that respect guillotine stages and saw constraints with minimum waste.
tasks.inputs: rectangular part list, board sizes, kerf, guillotine stage limits
tasks.outputs: cutting patterns and saw programs

crosswalk.scheme: Waescher et al. 2007 cutting and packing typology
crosswalk.label: Two-dimensional rectangular cutting stock problem

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the ROADEF/EURO 2018 glass-cutting challenge and classical guillotine instances give reference solutions

tasks.name: Linear cutting stock optimization
tasks.definition: Given required lengths of bars, tubes, extrusions or lumber and the stock lengths available, choose cutting patterns that minimize waste.
tasks.inputs: required lengths and quantities, stock lengths, kerf
tasks.outputs: cutting patterns and cut lists

crosswalk.scheme: Waescher et al. 2007 cutting and packing typology
crosswalk.label: One-dimensional cutting stock problem

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: BPPLIB and classic one-dimensional instances (Falkenauer, Scholl) have proven optima

tasks.name: Turret punch programming
tasks.definition: Given nested sheet parts and a punch press tool turret, assign tools to stations and sequence hits, nibbling and repositioning to avoid clamps.
tasks.inputs: nested layout, punch tool library, turret configuration, clamp positions
tasks.outputs: punch program with tool setup
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: hit count, tool changes and travel are scoreable, but machine constraints vary by vendor

tasks.name: Press brake bend programming
tasks.definition: Given a sheet-metal part, unfold it, choose bend sequence and tooling, set backgauge positions and check part-tool-machine collisions.
tasks.inputs: sheet-metal model, material, press brake and tool library
tasks.outputs: flat pattern, bend sequence, tool setup, press brake program
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: bend-sequence feasibility is checkable by collision simulation, but no public part set exists

tasks.name: Tube and profile cutting programming
tasks.definition: Given tubes or structural shapes with cut features, generate rotary laser or plasma cutting paths with bevels and nest parts along the stock length.
tasks.inputs: tube or profile part models, stock lengths, rotary cutter model
tasks.outputs: tube cutting program and length nest
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: path validity and stock use are computable in simulation, but machine models are proprietary

tasks.name: Wire electrical discharge machining programming
tasks.definition: Given 2D contours or ruled upper and lower profiles, generate two-axis and four-axis taper wire paths with skim cuts, tabs and threading points.
tasks.inputs: part contours or ruled surfaces, wire and machine technology tables
tasks.outputs: wire erosion program
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: contour offsets and taper geometry are checkable by simulation; technology tables are vendor-specific

tasks.name: Fabric marker making
tasks.definition: Given graded garment pattern pieces, fabric width and rules for grain, nap and pattern matching, nest pieces into a marker and generate the cutter program.
tasks.inputs: graded pattern pieces, size ratios, fabric width and properties, matching rules
tasks.outputs: marker layout, efficiency, knife-cutter program

crosswalk.scheme: Waescher et al. 2007 cutting and packing typology
crosswalk.label: Two-dimensional irregular strip packing

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ESICUP apparel instances (shirts, trousers) are standard irregular strip-packing benchmarks
tasks.notes: Pattern drafting and grading belong to design; nesting the graded pieces is production preparation.

capabilities.name: NC post-processing and verification
capabilities.definition: Given toolpaths or NC programs and a model of the machine and controller, produce controller-specific code, verify it by simulation, optimize it, and deliver it to the machine.

crosswalk.label: NC processor output: file structure and language format (CLDATA)
Data model for computerized numerical controllers

capabilities.notes: Was the post-processing half of the CAM seed. Post-processing is split by kinematics (two/three-axis versus five-axis transformation) because that is where post-processors differ in difficulty; multi-channel posting is covered in produce.turning_cam.multichannel_swiss.

tasks.name: Post-processor development
tasks.definition: Given a machine's kinematics, controller dialect and cycles, build and configure a post-processor that turns neutral toolpath data into that machine's code.
tasks.inputs: machine kinematic chain and limits, controller manual, sample programs
tasks.outputs: post-processor configuration or script
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: a post can be scored by round-tripping reference toolpaths through a machine simulator

tasks.name: Two and three-axis code generation
tasks.definition: Given toolpaths for a lathe or three-axis mill, emit controller code with correct arcs, canned cycles, compensation, tool changes and safe starts.
tasks.inputs: cutter location data, post-processor, controller dialect
tasks.outputs: controller program
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: output can be executed in an open controller interpreter and the resulting path compared with the source toolpath

tasks.name: Five-axis kinematic transformation
tasks.definition: Given tool positions and axis vectors, compute rotary and linear axis values for a table-table, head-head or head-table machine, choosing solutions, handling singularities and wrap, and linearizing large rotary moves.
tasks.inputs: tool position and orientation sequence, machine kinematics and limits
tasks.outputs: axis-space program with feed rates (including inverse-time)
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: axis solutions are exactly checkable from the kinematics, and singularity and wrap handling are scoreable on standard test paths

tasks.name: NC program verification by material removal
tasks.definition: Given an NC program, stock, tools and design model, simulate material removal and report gouges, excess stock and program errors.
tasks.inputs: NC program, stock, tool assemblies, design model
tasks.outputs: simulated in-process stock, deviation map, error list
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: deviation between simulated stock and the design model is computable, and programs with seeded errors make a test set

tasks.name: Machine collision simulation
tasks.definition: Given an NC program and a full machine model with fixtures and holders, simulate controller-level motion and report collisions, near misses and overtravel.
tasks.inputs: NC program, machine model, fixtures, tool assemblies
tasks.outputs: collision and overtravel report
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: collisions and overtravel on seeded test programs are exact pass or fail checks

tasks.name: Physics-based feed-rate optimization
tasks.definition: Given an NC program, tools and material, adjust feed per segment so that chip load or cutting force stays within limits while minimizing cycle time.
tasks.inputs: NC program, stock simulation, tool and material cutting model
tasks.outputs: optimized NC program, predicted cycle time and forces
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: cycle-time reduction is computable, but force limits need cutting-force models calibrated per material

tasks.name: Shop-floor and conversational programming
tasks.definition: Given a drawing at the machine, write or edit NC code by hand or through a controller's conversational dialogs, with backplot and checks.
tasks.inputs: part drawing, controller dialect or conversational cycles
tasks.outputs: edited or conversational NC program
onet_products: Computer numerical control CNC editor software
Computerized numerical control CNC programming software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: hand or machine-written G-code can be scored by simulation against a target part; conversational dialects are vendor-specific

tasks.name: NC program transfer and management
tasks.definition: Given approved NC programs and networked machines, deliver programs by DNC or file transfer, drip-feed large programs, and keep revisions and comparisons.
tasks.inputs: NC programs, machine connections, approval state
tasks.outputs: transferred programs, revision history
tasks.benchmarkable: no: a transfer and revision-control function whose only metric is correctness

capabilities.name: Additive manufacturing build preparation
capabilities.definition: Given 3D part models, an additive process and a machine, produce a validated build: repaired meshes, orientation, supports, layout and machine-specific layer or scan data.
capabilities.notes: Seed kept. Slicing tasks are split by the ISO/ASTM 52900 process categories that need different layer data (MEX, VPP, PBF, DED, jetting); sheet lamination has no distinct software in the inputs. Build-process distortion simulation is handed to simulate.

tasks.name: Build orientation and part packing
tasks.definition: Given parts and a build volume, choose each part's orientation (support volume, surface quality, height) and arrange them on the plate or in the powder volume.
tasks.inputs: part meshes, machine build volume, orientation criteria
tasks.outputs: oriented parts, build layout, packing density
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: packing density, build height and support volume are computable on shared part sets

tasks.name: Support structure generation
tasks.definition: Given an oriented part and process rules, detect overhangs and generate block, tree or lattice supports.
tasks.inputs: oriented mesh, overhang angle and process rules
tasks.outputs: support geometry
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: support volume and contact area are computable, but printability needs physical trials

tasks.name: Material extrusion slicing
tasks.definition: Given a mesh and printer and material profile, slice into layers and generate perimeters, infill, travel and temperatures as printer code.
tasks.inputs: mesh, printer profile, material profile
tasks.outputs: printer G-code, time and material estimate
onet_products: Fused deposition modeling FDM rapid prototyping systems
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: print time, material use and geometric fidelity of the toolpath are computable without printing

tasks.name: Vat photopolymerization slicing
tasks.definition: Given a supported mesh and resin profile, produce layer images or laser paths with exposure settings, hollowing and drain holes.
tasks.inputs: supported mesh, resin and printer profile
tasks.outputs: layer image stack or laser scan file
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: layer images are checkable against the mesh, but cure behaviour needs physical calibration

tasks.name: Powder bed fusion scan preparation
tasks.definition: Given a packed build, generate contour and hatch vectors, scan strategy (stripes, islands, rotation) and region parameters as a machine build file.
tasks.inputs: build layout, material parameter sets, machine specification
tasks.outputs: layer scan vectors and build file
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: vector coverage and scan time are computable; melt-pool quality needs simulation or trials

tasks.name: Directed energy deposition path planning
tasks.definition: Given a part or repair region, plan bead paths and deposition-head orientation for multi-axis wire or powder deposition, including non-planar layers.
tasks.inputs: part or repair geometry, bead model, multi-axis machine or robot
tasks.outputs: deposition toolpath
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: coverage and bead overlap are computable, but deposited geometry needs process models

tasks.name: Jetting build preparation
tasks.definition: Given multi-material or coloured models, assign materials and colours per voxel and produce halftoned layer images for material or binder jetting.
tasks.inputs: coloured or multi-material models, printer material set
tasks.outputs: per-layer droplet or binder images
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: colour and material placement are checkable against the model, but appearance needs printing

capabilities.name: Industrial robot programming
capabilities.definition: Given a work cell (robots, tools, fixtures, parts) and a process, produce executable robot programs with validated reach, collision-free motion, calibrated frames and acceptable cycle time.

crosswalk.label: Robot programming: teach programming and off-line programming
Level 1-2: sensing, manipulating and automated control

capabilities.notes: Seed 'Robot programming and offline simulation' kept and expanded. Tasks follow the steps a robot integrator performs (program, simulate, plan, sequence, calibrate, sense, safeguard). General mobile robotics has no owner in the brief; only industrial cells are modelled here.

tasks.name: Robot program authoring
tasks.definition: Given a cell and task description, write the robot program in the vendor language with frames, I/O handshakes and error recovery.
tasks.inputs: cell layout, task description, I/O list, frames
tasks.outputs: robot program (vendor language)
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: programs can run in vendor virtual controllers, but the languages are proprietary and benchmarks are only emerging

tasks.name: Offline programming and cell simulation
tasks.definition: Given 3D models of robots, tools, fixtures and parts, program and simulate the cell with a virtual controller to check reach, collisions and cycle time before download.
tasks.inputs: cell CAD, robot models, virtual controller, program
tasks.outputs: validated program, reach and cycle-time report
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: reach and cycle time are computable in simulation, but accuracy on the real cell depends on calibration

tasks.name: Collision-free motion planning
tasks.definition: Given robot kinematics, start and goal poses and the cell's obstacles, compute a collision-free, time-parameterized joint trajectory.
tasks.inputs: robot model, obstacle geometry, start and goal
tasks.outputs: joint trajectory
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: MotionBenchMaker and OMPL benchmarking score success rate, path quality and planning time

tasks.name: Process path generation
tasks.definition: Given part geometry and a process (arc or spot welding, painting, dispensing, deburring, machining), generate tool paths, orientations and process parameters for the robot.
tasks.inputs: part CAD with seams or surfaces, process tool, robot and positioner
tasks.outputs: robot process paths with parameters
onet_products: FANUC Robotics Through Arc Seam Tracking TAST
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: coverage uniformity and seam-following error are computable in simulation; process quality needs trials

tasks.name: Robot task sequencing and coordination
tasks.definition: Given many operations (welds, picks) and one or more robots with shared zones, allocate and order them to minimize cycle time without interference.
tasks.inputs: operation list with poses, robots, interference zones
tasks.outputs: per-robot sequences and interlocks, cycle time
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: the core is a generalized travelling-salesman problem with public instances, but cell interference constraints are not standardized

tasks.name: Robot and tool calibration
tasks.definition: Given measurements of the robot and tool, identify tool centre point, user frames, camera-to-robot transform and kinematic parameter corrections.
tasks.inputs: measured poses or images, nominal kinematics
tasks.outputs: calibrated tool, frames and kinematic parameters
onet_products: Tool center point TCP setting software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: residual pose error after calibration can be scored on simulated or published measurement sets against ISO 9283 criteria

tasks.name: Vision-guided picking
tasks.definition: Given 2D or 3D sensor data of parts in a tray or bin, estimate part poses, choose grasps and plan the approach.
tasks.inputs: images or point clouds, part models, gripper model
tasks.outputs: part poses, ranked grasps, pick trajectories
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the BOP 6D pose benchmark and GraspNet-1Billion score pose estimation and grasp quality

tasks.name: Robot safety configuration
tasks.definition: Given a risk assessment and cell layout, configure safe zones, tool and speed limits, and speed-and-separation or collaborative force limits in the robot safety controller.
tasks.inputs: risk assessment, cell layout, collaborative limits
tasks.outputs: safety controller configuration and validation report

crosswalk.label: Robots and robotic devices: safety requirements

onet_products: FANUC Robotics Dual Check Safety DCS Position and Speed Check
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: zone coverage against the risk assessment is geometrically checkable; validation is by certified testing
tasks.notes: Risk assessment itself belongs to operate.

capabilities.name: Programmable controller programming
capabilities.definition: Given a control specification and I/O list for a machine or process, author, test and deploy controller logic in the IEC 61131-3 or IEC 61499 languages.

crosswalk.label: Level 1-2: sensing, manipulating and automated control

capabilities.notes: Seed 'PLC and controller programming (IEC 61131-3)' kept. Tasks follow the IEC 61131-3 languages (IL is deprecated in the third edition and omitted), then motion, safety and verification, which practitioners treat as distinct work.

tasks.name: Ladder diagram programming
tasks.definition: Given interlock and sequence requirements, write relay-style ladder logic for a programmable controller.
tasks.inputs: control narrative, I/O list, interlock matrix
tasks.outputs: ladder program
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: programs run on open runtimes against I/O test vectors and can be model-checked

tasks.name: Structured text programming
tasks.definition: Given a control specification, write textual IEC 61131-3 code for calculations, state machines and data handling.
tasks.inputs: control specification, data types, I/O list
tasks.outputs: structured text program
onet_products: Programmable logic controller PLC code generation software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: LLM4PLC and Agents4PLC score generated structured text by compilation, simulation and model checking
tasks.notes: Code generated from block-diagram models lands here.

tasks.name: Function block diagram programming
tasks.definition: Given a control specification, wire standard and user function blocks graphically for continuous and logic control.
tasks.inputs: control specification, block library
tasks.outputs: function block diagram program
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: programs execute on runtimes, but graphical sources are hard to exchange outside PLCopen XML

tasks.name: Sequential function chart programming
tasks.definition: Given a machine cycle, express it as steps, transitions and actions with parallel and alternative branches.
tasks.inputs: machine sequence description, I/O list
tasks.outputs: sequential function chart
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: sequence behaviour is checkable by model checking or simulation against the specified cycle

tasks.name: Distributed function block applications
tasks.definition: Given a control application spanning several devices, model it as event-driven IEC 61499 function block networks and map them to devices.
tasks.inputs: application specification, device topology
tasks.outputs: IEC 61499 application and device mapping
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: applications run on open runtimes, but few reference applications exist

tasks.name: Motion control and drive configuration
tasks.definition: Given axis mechanics and motion requirements, configure servo and frequency drives, program PLCopen motion blocks, cams and electronic gearing, and tune axes.
tasks.inputs: axis mechanics, motor and drive data, motion profile
tasks.outputs: drive parameters, motion program, tuning
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: cam profiles and gearing are checkable in simulation; axis tuning needs the physical axis

tasks.name: Safety interlock logic programming
tasks.definition: Given a cause-and-effect matrix and safety requirements, program safety controller or instrumented-system logic with voting, bypass and reset handling.
tasks.inputs: cause-and-effect matrix, safety requirements specification
tasks.outputs: safety logic program and test records

crosswalk.label: Safety instrumented systems for the process industry

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: logic can be checked against the cause-and-effect matrix by model checking; certification is not benchmarkable
tasks.notes: Safety integrity level determination and verification belong to operate.

tasks.name: Control logic verification and virtual commissioning
tasks.definition: Given controller code and a simulated machine or plant, test and formally verify the logic before startup.
tasks.inputs: controller program, plant or machine emulation, requirements
tasks.outputs: test results, counterexamples, commissioning report
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: seeded-fault detection on reference programs and plant models gives a score

capabilities.name: Supervisory and process control
capabilities.definition: Given a running plant with field instruments and controllers, show its state to operators, acquire and archive data, raise alarms, and compute regulatory and advanced control actions.

crosswalk.label: Level 2: monitoring, supervisory control and automated control
Human Machine Interfaces for Process Automation Systems

capabilities.notes: Seed 'SCADA, HMI and distributed process control on the plant floor' kept as one capability: ISA-95 Level 2. Utility-network SCADA (EMS, DMS, OMS) and building automation go to operate per the brief. Control-law design is simulate's; tuning and deploying controllers on a running plant is here.

tasks.name: Operator display design
tasks.definition: Given a process and its tags, build overview and detail displays, faceplates and navigation following high-performance HMI practice.
tasks.inputs: process diagrams, tag list, display standards
tasks.outputs: HMI screens and faceplates
onet_products: GE Intelligent Platforms Proficy HMI/SCADA iFIX
